text: EOS-04, formerly known as RISAT-1A, is an Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) radar imaging satellite designed to provide high-quality images under all weather and lighting conditions, supporting applications in Agriculture, Forestry & Plantations, Soil Moisture & Hydrology, and Flood mapping. It is a follow-on to the RISAT-1 satellite with a similar configuration and is the sixth in the RISAT series. Equipped with a C-band synthetic-aperture radar (SAR), the satellite has a liftoff mass of 1,710 kg (3,770 lb) and operates in a polar, Sun-synchronous orbit at an altitude of approximately 529 km, passing at 06:00 AM Local Day Night (LTDN). The satellite complements data from Resourcesat, Cartosat, and the RISAT-2B series. Assembly, integration, and testing were conducted by a consortium led by Alpha Design Technologies Ltd. The approximate cost of EOS-04 is ₹490 crore, equivalent to ₹550 crore or US$65 million in 2023. EOS-04 was launched on 14 February 2022 at 05:59 hrs IST (00:29 hrs UTC) via the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV-C52) from the First Launch Pad (FLP) at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC), Sriharikota. The launch included two rideshare satellites: INS-2TD, an ISRO technology demonstrator, and INSPIREsat-1, a university satellite. The satellite captured its first images on 25 February 2022 following launch.
